brief: BofA's Back to School update lifts 2026 global growth to 3.3% (+10bp vs mid-year) and trims 2027 to 3.4% (-10bp), with 2028 at 3.3%. The chain: the US AI investment boom plus an Asian export cycle running near 30% yoy offsets the energy shock and the Iran war, so growth holds, but persistent inflation and AI-related demand for capital push long-term rates up, tightening financial conditions, which BofA treats as a further negative supply shock for the world ex-US and a risk to the AI-driven equity rally via wealth effects. Global inflation is revised to 2.5% in 2027 (+10bp) on stickier developed-market prices and higher energy forecasts (Brent averaging $83/bbl in 2H26, $75 in 2027). BofA keeps an out-of-consensus call for 75bp of Fed hikes this year starting September, arguing the Fed cannot credibly hold barring a very soft August CPI and that a hold risks sharply higher long-end yields. The ECB hiked 25bp and may be done, with December risk rising, and market pricing of five hikes judged too hawkish. The BoE is seen on hold 6-3 with QT slowed to 50bn. China 2027 growth is marked down to 4.2%.
